exposure: Mode of delivery (Vaginal Delivery, Cesarean Section, Elective CS, Emergency CS in first stage, Emergency CS in second stage)
cohort: The study included postpartum mothers at a Nigerian tertiary hospital.
finding: Vaginal delivery was associated with a significantly higher risk of both urinary and anal incontinence compared to cesarean section overall.
mod_finding: Elective and early-stage emergency cesarean sections reduced the risk of urinary and anal incontinence, while vaginal delivery and emergency cesarean section in the second stage of labor increased it.
